players.product: long-haul / middle-mile fiber construction for hyperscaler data-center interconnect

quarterly_data.quarter: Dycom 25th annual diversified industrials & services conference 2026 (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO on constraints: on the communications side 'labor is not a constraining factor for us' today - 'the constraint today on the communication side comes down to permitting'. Industry-wide, 'as you start to get to 2028, you are going to have labor constraints', with a 'huge balloon of all this activity starting in 2028' that he believes will push many builds out over a longer horizon. Customers are securing fiber through partnerships with Corning, and 'there could be fiber shortages for people that haven't done that'; the equipment landscape looks able to meet the need. Electricians are 'absolutely a bottleneck' keeping the flow of data-center builds restrained. Moving a fiber-to-the-home worker to long-haul / middle-mile takes 'at least six months of training'.
quarterly_data.figure: communications constraint is permitting, not labor; industry labor constraints from 2028; possible fiber shortages for those without secured supply; at least six months of long-haul retraining

quarterly_data.quarter: Dycom 25th annual diversified industrials & services conference 2026 (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO on data-center demand: as of a check 'two days ago', 'absolutely no change. Still massive demand, still massive velocity'; moratoriums have no direct impact today because those projects 'have not even got to permitting yet' and are years out. 'Not all data centers are AI data centers' - Dycom is building AI data centers today but positions itself on data creation and cloud growth with 'AI upside'. He says the $20 billion long-haul / middle-mile market 'is just going to be the starting point', a 'very long arc curve'; the over $1 billion long-haul backlog is 'literally just fiber connecting data centers nationwide'.
quarterly_data.figure: no change in data-center demand; $20 billion addressable market 'the starting point'

quarterly_data.quarter: Dycom 25th annual diversified industrials & services conference 2026 (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO on mix and margins: fiscal 2027 organic growth of 10%-12% is 'all coming through the telecommunications business', coming off 'a $5.4 billion communications year last year'. Service and maintenance is about half of Dycom's revenue, around $3 billion plus or minus on communications, with a different growth curve from program work. Communications adjusted EBITDA margin is in a '±13% range' this year (13.3% last year), with operating leverage possible as it grows. Building Systems is about 20% of the mix today (80/20) and he expects that share to grow larger through organic growth and selective M&A.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 organic growth 10%-12%; communications $5.4 billion last year; service and maintenance around $3 billion; communications margin ±13%; Building Systems about 20% of mix

quarterly_data.quarter: Dycom 25th annual diversified industrials & services conference 2026 (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO on Building Systems: reported backlog 'is always going to be an understated number' because data centers are contracted 'just in time by phases'; customer conversations 'at the earliest, are two years out, but more like three and four years out', and a new set of data centers can mean 'five, six, eight years of total build cycle'. Power Solutions (electrical connections powering racks) and National Technology Integrators (cabling and fiber back to the meet-me room) are working on the same sites, and Dycom is cross-selling inside-the-fence and carrier work. Further M&A will focus on the Building Systems side, with geographic expansion the priority.
quarterly_data.figure: Building Systems customer conversations two to four years out; data-center build cycles of five, six, eight years
